summary: Gate of batch-measurement: 2 questions on r69 and r74 (adds r68-r74, removes r50).
questions: batch-measurement r69: how is the field `ok` named? (a, recommended) In the Behaviour line, as drafted: [r69] "The JSON object that `measure` gives shall hold the field `ok`." (b) The line says what `ok` means and names `ok` only in Implementation: "The JSON object that `measure` gives shall hold whether `measure` did what it was asked." The other lines drafted stand either way: [r68] "`measure` shall give its output as one JSON object on stdout." [r70] "**When** `measure` does what it was asked, `measure` shall give `ok` true in its JSON object." [r71] "**When** `measure` ends without crashing on an error it does not handle, `measure` shall exit successfully." [r72] "**If** `measure` crashes on an error it does not handle, **then** `measure` shall exit with an error." [r73] "**If** `measure` refuses, **then** `measure` shall give `ok` false in its JSON object, with the reason it refuses." Removed: [r50] "**If** `measure` refuses, **then** `measure` shall exit with an error." (replaced by r73).

batch-measurement r74: [r74] "**When** `measure show` or `measure compare` is run, `measure` shall give the text of its tables inside a field of its JSON object." The note names three text commands (the SessionStart hook, features showing Gherkin, model rules), not `measure show` or `compare`. (a, recommended) Keep r74: the tables are read as text, so they go inside a field. (b) Drop r74: `measure show` and `compare` give their tables as JSON data only.
